title: Empty a vacuum's dust cup through its bottom flap into the bin and click it back in
instruction: Empty the vacuum cleaner's dust cup into the bin and put the cup back on the vacuum.
context: The ability: open a container's own trapdoor only over the bin, then latch the container back onto a sloped catch. Bagless vacuum cups are emptied this way between rooms; dirt let out anywhere else is spilled. Done by: janitors, housekeeping cleaners and home care aides (O*NET 37-2011, 37-2012, 31-1122). Unlike TK-DHVTXV (lift lint off a screen, slide it back), TK-G8EZFC (swap a filter under a sprung cover) and TK-6FB8W7 (tip a cell out of a box), the dirt leaves through the cup's own door.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Vacuum body (fixed, grey plastic): a block 120 mm front to back, 130 mm wide and 92 mm tall, centred 33 cm in front of the arm bases, its right face 2.9 cm left of the midline, with a dark vent strip on top. To its right, a dark tray: a 5 mm floor 128 x 120 mm and 15 mm walls 6 mm thick at the front, back and right, centred 33 cm in front and 2.8 cm right of the midline. Catch (yellow): a tongue 40 mm wide, 34 mm long and 6 mm thick reaching out of the block's right face over the cup's left rim, its last 10 mm black, its underside 86 mm up, and a post 20 x 10 x 32 mm on the block's top 14 cm left of the midline; pushing the post 22 mm to the left pulls the tongue back clear of the rim (spring 40 N/m). A cup coming down onto the tongue pushes it back and it springs over the rim. Dust cup (loose, 0.2 kg), docked in the tray, centred 33 cm in front and 2.5 cm right of the midline: clear (tinted, see-through) plastic walls 70 x 70 x 80 mm, 5 mm thick, on a grey flange 100 x 100 x 4 mm, so its underside is 5 mm up and its rim 85 mm up; two grey grille bars 9 mm wide across its top, front to back; on its right rim a dark handle bar 50 mm long, 12 mm wide, standing 30 mm above the rim, with a red button 16 x 8 x 8 mm on top. Its bottom is a flap 60 x 60 x 5 mm hinged at its far edge: while the button is held pressed 4 mm or more the flap is driven open to 1.0 rad (57 degrees); letting go springs it shut, and it latches. Dirt: three bright orange balls 16 mm across, 10 g each, on the flap, 14 mm nearer the robot and 21 mm right of the cup's centre, 12 mm farther than its centre, and 10 mm nearer and 21 mm left of its centre. Bin (fixed, black plastic): an open box 92 x 92 mm and 60 mm tall with 8 mm walls (a 76 mm opening), centred 22 cm in front and 16 cm right of the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end, after the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of the cup, the balls or the catch), with everything still for 1 s. A ball is in the cup when its centre is inside the cup's walls (in any orientation); in the bin when its centre is inside the bin's inner walls, below its rim, and not in the cup. Docked: the cup's underside within 1 mm of the tray floor, upright within 3 degrees, its centre within 8 mm front to back and 7 mm sideways of the tray's centre. 1.0: all three balls in the bin, the cup docked with the catch's tongue back over its rim (within 1 mm of its rest) and the flap shut (within 3 degrees). 0.5: all three balls in the bin and the cup anywhere else on the table, tray or bin. 0.25: the cup out of the tray, upright within 10 degrees, all three balls still in it. 0 otherwise, including the cup on the floor. 0 for the whole trial, judged from the video, if at any point a ball lands on the table, the tray, the vacuum body or the floor, or lies still anywhere outside the cup and the bin.
reset_notes: Put the three balls back on the flap at their spots, shut the flap until it latches, and press the cup down into the tray until the catch springs over its rim. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: A scaled mock-up. Real cups are closed under the cyclone; here a grille closes the top and the walls are see-through. The flap is driven open while the button is held and springs shut when let go. The catch responds to the cup's position: it pulls back as a cup comes down onto it (its sloped face) and springs over the rim once the cup is home. Masses and friction are simulator values. One fixed layout.
